request.spec:
Selected claims can be voided together: a reason select (when the sheet has void reasons) and a
button beside the bulk buttons; each selected claim is voided in list order exactly as the row's
void does (with its CLAIM_VOIDED and rollup lines); show how many were voided and how many
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be voided together: a reason select (when the sheet has void reasons) and a
button beside the bulk buttons; each selected claim is voided in list order exactly as the row's
void does (with its CLAIM_VOIDED and rollup lines); show how many were voided and how many
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk void is in place, and all 4 acceptance tests pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

**What was added:** one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/claims/bulkVoid.slot.tsx`. The app finds it automatically and shows it with the other bulk buttons, just after "Re-date selected". It has:
- **A void-reason dropdown** (`bulk-void-reason`), shown only when the sheet has void reasons.
- **A "Void selected" button** (`bulk-void`).
- **The result** ("Voided N, refused M", in `bulk-voided` and `bulk-void-refused`). It clears when the button is pressed again or the reason changes.

**How it works:** it voids the ticked claims one at a time in list order: people in their list order, newest claim first within each person. Each void goes through the same server call as the row's Void button, with the chosen reason. So every rule that applies to a single void still applies, and each claim writes its own `CLAIM_VOIDED` and rollup audit lines. These include the rule that only a steward can void a settled claim, and that a reason is required once the sheet has void reasons. A claim the server refuses stays as it is and counts as refused. Afterwards the ticks and the chosen reason are cleared.

**What it doesn't do:** there is no all-or-nothing check. If some claims are refused, the rest are still voided, which is how the existing bulk re-date behaves. No server or database changes were needed.
